html:
Epicureanism is the school of philosophy founded by Epicurus in Athens around 307 BCE. It taught that the good life is a pleasant one, and that the highest pleasure is peace of mind and freedom from pain.

The school met in Epicurus's Garden, which was open to women and slaves. Its members lived together simply, valued friendship above almost everything, and kept out of politics; one of their mottoes was "live unnoticed". Later followers summed up the teaching as a fourfold cure: do not fear the gods, do not worry about death, what is good is easy to get, and what is terrible is easy to endure.

It rested on atomism. If the world is only atoms and void and the soul ends at death, there is nothing to fear. That made it a rival to Plato's followers and above all to Stoicism.

It spread to Rome, where Lucretius wrote On the Nature of Things. Christians later attacked it, and "epicure" came to mean a lover of luxury, which Epicurus was not. It revived in the 17th century, and Thomas Jefferson once called himself an Epicurean.
sum: Epicureanism is the school of philosophy founded by Epicurus in Athens around 307 BCE. It taught that the good life is a pleasant one, and that the highest pleasure is peace of mind and freedom from pain.
